behavior: gh is authenticated on ace2 and works from a NON-interactive shell, not only a login shell (the f4 lesson from ANSIBLE-028: shell class matters)
verification: ssh ace2 'gh auth status' && ssh ace2 'gh api /user --jq .login'

behavior: An agent inside a tmux session clones a private repo, commits, pushes a branch and opens a PR with no human and no agent forwarding; the test artefacts are cleaned up afterwards
verification: ssh ace2 'tmux new-session -d -s acceptance-f2 "set -e; cd /tmp && rm -rf f2 && gh repo clone mlorentedev/kubelab f2 -- --depth 1 && cd f2 && git checkout -b acceptance/ansible-033-$$ && date > .acceptance-probe && git add -A && git commit -m \"test(ANSIBLE-033): acceptance probe\" && git push -u origin HEAD && gh pr create --fill --draft > /tmp/f2.url && gh pr close --delete-branch \$(cat /tmp/f2.url) && echo F2_OK > /tmp/f2.result"' && sleep 60 && ssh ace2 'grep -q F2_OK /tmp/f2.result'

behavior: The token is fine-grained (not classic) and its refused permissions are actually refused — a workflow-file push is rejected by GitHub
verification: ssh ace2 'gh auth token | grep -q "^github_pat_"' && ssh ace2 'gh api -X GET /user/starred --silent'
evidence: NOTE at authoring time: the `github_pat_` prefix distinguishes fine-grained from classic (`ghp_`) and IS executable. The 90-day expiry and the All-repositories scope are NOT machine-readable from the API for fine-grained PATs — they are confirmed by inspecting the token's settings page, and that manual step is part of this criterion rather than pretended to be automated. Do not mark this feature verified on the executable half alone.

behavior: The credential is delivered reproducibly by the dev_node role from SOPS common, and provisioning converges: a second pass reports changed=0 with no task flipping to changed
verification: make provision NODE=ace2 ENV=staging TAGS=dev_node | tee /tmp/c1 && make provision NODE=ace2 ENV=staging TAGS=dev_node | tee /tmp/c2 && grep -qE 'changed=0 .*failed=0' /tmp/c2

behavior: No prod credential is reachable from ace2. The age-key absence is the load-bearing part: per SEC-SOPS-001 (#889) any age key on this node would decrypt prod, so this criterion guards the assumption the whole spec rests on
verification: ssh ace2 '! test -e ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt && ! test -e ~/.age/key.txt && ! test -e /etc/sops/age.key && ! command -v sops >/dev/null && ! ls ~/.kube/*prod* 2>/dev/null'

behavior: The token never lands in a process argument, a log line, or a world-readable file; gh owns it in its own credential store
verification: grep -rn 'no_log: true' infra/ansible/roles/dev_node/tasks/main.yml && ! grep -rEn 'gh auth login .*--with-token[^|]*\$\{?dev_node_github_token' infra/ansible/roles/dev_node/tasks/main.yml && ssh ace2 'test "$(stat -c %a ~/.config/gh)" -le 700'

behavior: Expiry day is a scheduled event, not a mystery outage: a rotation runbook exists naming the failure symptom, the mint/re-provision/revoke sequence, and a prompt to reconsider the repository scope
verification: test -f docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi '401' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi 'revoke' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md && grep -qi 'repository access' docs/runbooks/dev-node-token-rotation.md
